title: while and do while: finite streams and termination
goal: Distinguish testing before and after the body and explain how each iteration advances through input.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–2: expressions, comparisons, types, references, and checked cin.
Follow the prerequisite links: cpp.for-loop. New constructs are introduced before the assignment.

sections.title: Pre-test and post-test loops
paragraphs: Imagine a button counter. If the button is already released, while may do nothing. If a menu must be shown first, the first action belongs before the test. That difference appears in the output 0 1.

while(condition) tests before the body and can execute zero times. do {body} while(condition); tests after the body and executes at least once. The final semicolon is required for do while; after a regular while it usually creates an unintended empty body.

Choose according to the contract. A sequence should be processed only when another value exists, making while(std::cin>>x) natural. A mandatory initial action may use do while, but this never justifies using an unread x.

sections.title: A mandatory first step
paragraphs: Both loops use false. Locate each test relative to ++ and predict the two counters.

sections.title: Reading is a progress operation
paragraphs: In while(cin>>x), successful extraction supplies a new value and enters the body. Failure stops before x is used. Testing !cin.eof() before reading is wrong: eof reports an already encountered end rather than predicting the next extraction’s success.

When a condition contains only a flag, the body must update it or obtain new data. Ensure continue cannot skip the next progress operation. Even Nexus’s finite input cannot rescue a loop that has stopped consuming it.
With 2 3 0 99, extraction changes both value and the stream position. After reading 0, 99 stays unread because break ends the loop.

sections.title: EOF, a sentinel, and a limit
paragraphs: EOF is the end of the supplied buffer; a sentinel such as 0 means stop under the task’s rules. The sentinel is consumed but usually excluded from the sum. State explicitly whether data after it is rejected or ignored.

A count limit bounds memory and time even for valid input. The lab permits at most 100 nonzero measurements with magnitude at most 1000, so the absolute sum cannot exceed 100000. Check the limit before changing the result.
A sentinel is a data contract. The example leaves the suffix after 0 unchecked. In the independent task only whitespace may follow 0.

sections.title: A stream up to a sentinel
paragraphs: Read 2, 3, 0 and 99 in order. Stop at the first point where the program knows its result.

reveal.title: Reveal output and trace execution
paragraphs: The output is the count of accepted values and their sum. This example does not require consuming the remaining input after the sentinel.

tables.caption: Trace for this run
rows: This is a valid value, not the sentinel.

sections.title: Classify extraction failure
paragraphs: After extraction stops, determine why. For the lab’s constrained short integers, an exhausted remainder is normal EOF and a letter is malformed input. With arbitrary tokens, fail and eof may both be set for an invalid or oversized number.

Preserve the distinction by first consuming allowed whitespace and checking EOF, then attempting extraction. If a token exists but extraction fails, reject it even if eof=true. Full line parsing and recovery are developed in the stream-state lesson.

Compare an empty stream with the token x. The first means there are no more values; the second means the attempted value is not an integer. The loop test can be false in both cases, yet the required results differ.

sections.title: A stream invariant
paragraphs: Before each step, count is the number of accepted values, sum is their sum, and the buffer begins with unprocessed input. Validate the range before adding. On rejection, produce invalid rather than a partially successful answer.

Termination follows from consuming the remaining finite buffer on each successful read and explicitly handling failure. A sentinel stops earlier. Waiting for more input may be normal in an interactive terminal; Nexus supplies the whole stdin buffer before execution.
Before reading the next token, count covers only accepted nonzero values and sum is their total. The sentinel ends extraction without changing either.

sections.title: Choosing and checking the form
paragraphs: Use for for a known n and while for input until EOF or stop. do while suits repetition after one mandatory initial action. Do not simulate a live menu by waiting for input absent from the supplied buffer.

Test empty input, a sentinel alone, one value, normal EOF, a letter, and an oversized numeric token. Keep a count/sum trace. Next, extract the computation into a function so input handling and calculation can be tested separately.
A huge final token is still invalid even at end of file. Determine whether a next token exists, then validate its complete spelling and range.

sections.title: Now try your own task
paragraphs: Build a strict sensor report. Validate values before the sentinel, then make sure no further records follow it.
Separate end of input, the sentinel, a malformed token and a valid value.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the shown example print for 2 3 0 99?

options: Yes, when its first condition is false
selfcheck.feedback: do while requires the first iteration; while does not.

selfcheck.prompt: Is sentinel 0 included in the lab sum?
selfcheck.feedback: Consuming it and processing it as data are different actions.

options: Success consumes input and failure terminates
selfcheck.feedback: The remaining finite buffer must decrease.

selfcheck.prompt: Does eof prove an oversized final number valid?
options: No; fail may also be set

selfcheck.prompt: What is needed to accept this lab?
options: Source, actual results, original tests, and a contract explanation
selfcheck.feedback: A progress flag is not evidence of independent mastery.

selfcheck.prompt: Why must the lab reject 2 0 3 even though the worked example stops immediately after 0? Where should the tail be checked?
selfcheck.feedback: Check the remaining input separately after the sentinel. A huge token must produce invalid even at EOF.

practice.title: Stop and check the remainder
practice.task: Sum at most 100 nonzero integers from −1000 through 1000 until EOF or the sentinel 0. Only whitespace may follow 0. Print the count and sum separated by a space. Print invalid for a bad token, out-of-range value, excess count or trailing token.
criteria: Compare 2 3, 2 3 0 and 2 3 0 99. The last input must be rejected by the lab.
Every repetition either consumes input or terminates.
An oversized final number can set both fail and eof. eof alone does not prove a token was valid.
Add two cases of your own, including a rejection if the interface allows one. Explain one boundary result.
Keep the source, exact input and observed output.
practice.hint: Check the remaining input separately after the sentinel. A huge token must produce invalid even at EOF.

steps.action: Separate end of input, the sentinel, a malformed token and a valid value.
Advance one token at a time. After validating the token and its range, increment the counter only for a nonzero value.
Compare 2 3, 2 3 0 and 2 3 0 99. The last input must be rejected by the lab.

terms.definition: a value that terminates a sequence under its contract.
a state set after the end of input has been encountered.
the condition is checked before the body.
the condition is checked after a mandatory initial body.
a change reducing the remaining work.
a supplied buffer with a detectable end.
